## Why? {#why}

**Research question:** Which prototype is fastest to use in which task, and where do people give up?

A table of means does not reveal that some times stick to the 180 s timeout, or that a line through all points suggests a relationship that does not exist within the conditions. A plot shows distribution, outliers and patterns before you calculate anything, and in a report it is often the first thing readers look at. ggplot2 builds every plot from the same few building blocks.

## Concept {#concept}

```{=html}
<figure class="rt-figure">
<svg viewBox="0 0 560 190" role="img" aria-labelledby="fig-vi-title fig-vi-desc" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <title id="fig-vi-title">Building blocks of a ggplot</title>
  <desc id="fig-vi-desc">Four building blocks joined by plus signs: ggplot with data and aes sets the data and mappings that all layers inherit. Then come layers such as geom_boxplot and geom_hline, then facets and scales. Below, the note: aes maps columns, values outside aes are fixed settings.</desc>
  <rect x="10" y="30" width="170" height="60" rx="6" class="rt-fig-box-accent" />
  <rect x="200" y="30" width="150" height="60" rx="6" class="rt-fig-box" />
  <rect x="370" y="30" width="180" height="60" rx="6" class="rt-fig-box" />
  <text x="95" y="55" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-code">ggplot(data, aes())</text>
  <text x="95" y="76" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label rt-fig-muted">data, mappings</text>
  <text x="275" y="55" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-code">+ geom_*()</text>
  <text x="275" y="76" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label rt-fig-muted">layers</text>
  <text x="460" y="50" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-code">+ facet_*()</text>
  <text x="460" y="66" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-code">+ scale_*()</text>
  <text x="460" y="83" text-anchor="middle" class="rt-fig-label rt-fig-muted">panels, axes</text>
  <text x="10" y="130" class="rt-fig-code">aes(fill = prototype)</text>
  <text x="200" y="130" class="rt-fig-label">Mapping: value comes from a column, with legend</text>
  <text x="10" y="160" class="rt-fig-code">fill = "steelblue"</text>
  <text x="200" y="160" class="rt-fig-label">Setting: one fixed value for all, outside aes()</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>What is in <code>ggplot(aes())</code> is inherited by all layers. What is in <code>geom_*(aes())</code> applies only there.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

- **Data in long format:** every variable that should go on x, colour or panels is a column (lesson "Reshaping").
- **`aes()` (mapping)** maps columns to aesthetics: `x`, `y`, `colour`, `fill`, `group`. Each mapping gets a scale with a legend.
- **Setting:** fixed values (`alpha = 0.4`, `fill = "steelblue"`, `linetype = "dashed"`) go outside `aes()`.
- **Layers** (`geom_point()`, `geom_boxplot()`, `geom_col()`, `geom_smooth()`, `geom_hline()`) are stacked on top of each other in the order of the code.
- **Facets** split into panels (`facet_wrap(~condition)`), **scales** control axes and colours (`scale_x_log10()`).
- **Summarise before plotting:** compute means and error bars with `summarise()`, with the person as the unit.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## More: plots for the report

- Show individual values where possible (points over box plots) instead of only bars with error bars.
- Label axes with units: `labs(x = NULL, y = "Task time (s)", fill = "Prototype")`.
- Calm theme: `theme_minimal(base_size = 12)`; colours for colour vision deficiency: `scale_fill_viridis_d()`.
- Save locally with `ggsave("fig1.png", width = 16, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300)`.
:::

## Example {#example}

Task times by task and prototype, individual values over the boxes. Change `fill` to `colour` or remove `geom_point()` and run the code again:

```{webr}
ggplot(usability, aes(task, time_s, fill = prototype)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15, dodge.width = 0.75),
    alpha = 0.3, size = 1
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Task time (s)", fill = "Prototype") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

Means with error bars: first average per person, then across people.

```{webr}
seq_summary <- usability |>
  summarise(seq = mean(seq, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(participant, prototype)) |>
  summarise(m = mean(seq), se = sd(seq) / sqrt(n()), n = n(), .by = prototype)
seq_summary

ggplot(seq_summary, aes(prototype, m)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = m - se, ymax = m + se), width = 0.15) +
  labs(x = "Prototype", y = "Ease (SEQ, 1–7), M ± SE") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

**How to report it (figure caption):** Figure 1. Mean ease rating (SEQ, 1–7) by prototype; error bars show ± 1 standard error across people (n = 24, for C n = 23).

## Package comparison {#packages}

| Task | Recommended | Alternative |
|---|---|---|
| Statistical graphics | **ggplot2** | Base R `plot()`, `boxplot()`: quick for a first look, hard to combine and style |
| Several plots in one figure | **patchwork** (`p1 + p2`) | `cowplot::plot_grid()` |
| Plotting model results | **see** (`plot(estimate_means(...))`) | `ggeffects` |
| Interactive graphics | `plotly::ggplotly()` | web only, not for the paper |

## Cheat sheet {#cheatsheet}

```r
ggplot(usability, aes(task, time_s, fill = prototype)) +   # data + mappings (inherited)
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +                       # layer
  geom_hline(yintercept = 180, linetype = "dashed") +      # reference, fixed value
  facet_wrap(~expertise) +                                 # panels
  scale_y_log10() +                                        # scale
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Time (s)", fill = "Prototype") +
  theme_minimal()

# error bars: person as the unit
rt_summary <- driving_sim |>
  summarise(rt_ms = mean(rt_ms, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(participant, condition)) |>
  summarise(m = mean(rt_ms), se = sd(rt_ms) / sqrt(n()), .by = condition)
```

- Column → inside `aes()`; fixed value → outside.
- Shared mappings in `ggplot(aes())`, otherwise `geom_smooth()` does not know the groups.
- `geom_col()` for precomputed values, `geom_bar()` counts rows; side by side with `position = "dodge"`.
- Log axis with `scale_x_log10()`, not `aes(x = log10(...))`.
